newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin rules out printing money.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin rules out printing money.

text.p: The Russian government believes a big increase in money supply would cause hyper-inflation and rejects the idea as a solution to Russia's fiscal problems, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday.
But Chernomyrdin told the State Duma lower house of parliament that money supply was already growing faster than inflation and would continue to do so.

Communist deputies have proposed an emergency issue of money, doubling money supply to about 600 trillion roubles, to eliminate a shortage of funds which prevents the government and many enterprises from paying their bills.

But Chernomyrdin, reporting to the Duma on the performance of the budget so far this year, said a big increase in money supply would re-ignite inflation, widen the budget deficit and cause the rouble to crash.
"The government and above all the central bank are carrying out a policy to control monetary emission which is aimed at lowering interest rates," Chernomyrdin told the Duma.
He said the government would not approve a substantial increase in money supply.
"Such decisions are completely unacceptable for us today."
Chernomyrdin noted that growth in money supply is in any case running above inflation.
Prices rose over the whole of 1996 by 22 percent, while money supply grew 34 percent, he said.
In the first four months of this year, prices have risen about six percent while money supply has grown 11 percent.
Inflation is forecast at 12 percent this year, against a 30 percent planned rise in money supply, he said.
A shortfall in budgeted revenues, partly caused by the lack of cash in the economy, is forcing the government to propose sharp cuts in this year's planned spending.
